alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ rendered by the verse-initial For.
Ordinary negator aligned to not; no second negative word competes, so rules 41 and 59 do not apply.

The Greek clause is verbless and its predicate is the prepositional phrase διὰ νόμου, so under rule 53 the supplied copula was rides with the preposition, discontinuously under rule 15, and is not read off the ASV's word order onto the subject noun ἐπαγγελία. Head on through under rule 62's closing clause.

Anarthrous Greek noun with a supplied determiner: under rule 51's anarthrous clause the supplied the is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun, since no article stands to take it. The ASV's margin Or, through law confirms the article is not in the Greek.
Article surfacing as English the under rule 19.
Bare subject noun; the supplied copula belongs to the prepositional predicate under rule 53, not to the subject.
Article before a name with no English determiner: rule 23. Under rule 21's determinerless clause the case preposition to stays with the name rather than leaving a bare to on the article.
Dative name taking its case preposition under rule 21's determinerless clause; head on the name under rule 17.
Disjunctive particle.
The genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ occupies the English determiner slot, so the article is displaced under rule 20; the ASV supplies it no word of any other kind.
Dative noun with its case preposition riding along under rule 21's determinerless clause, the article having been displaced; discontinuous around his under rule 15.
Genitive pronoun carrying the English possessive under rule 20.

Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive: rule 61, English spelling the construction with no word answering to the article itself. No preposition governs it, so the supplied complementizer that is not drawn onto the article; giving that to the article instead of to the infinitive remains a defensible reading, but rule 61 and rule 85 place a supplied complementizer on the non-finite complement the ASV expands into a finite clause.
Predicate accusative noun, bare.
The accusative subject of the infinitive is expressed in the Greek, so under rule 74 it takes the English subject word as its own unit and nothing is supplied.

The infinitive keeps the supplied complementizer that under rule 85 and the modal auxiliary should under rule 9, headed on the lexical verb be under rules 9 and 17; discontinuous around the expressed subject he under rule 15. Textual unit SBLGNT.ROM.4.13.v009 is underdetermined over this token and the projection carries r00-base, which rule 12 leaves as given.
Anarthrous genitive noun rendered of + noun: the case preposition and the supplied determiner are rule 7 helpers on the noun under rule 51's anarthrous clause, and rule 17 heads the unit on the noun.
Adversative conjunction.
Second occurrence of διά; the ASV supplies no second copula here, so this unit takes only through.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied determiner under rule 51's anarthrous clause; head on the noun.
Genitive noun rendered of + noun, headed on the noun under rule 17.

review_notes: Verbless clause: the supplied was is given to the prepositional predicate διά under rule 53 rather than to the subject noun, against the ASV's word order, which rule 53 refuses as a test.
Both articles left unrepresented are so for distinct reasons — s007 before a name with no determiner (rules 23, 21), s010 displaced by αὐτοῦ (rule 20) — and neither is grouped with its noun.

Anarthrous νόμου, κόσμου, δικαιοσύνης and πίστεως take their supplied determiners and case prepositions as rule 7 helpers, no Greek article standing to claim them (rule 51's anarthrous clause; rule 21).

The articular infinitive is split three ways: article unrepresented (rule 61), expressed accusative subject on αὐτόν (rule 74), complementizer and modal on εἶναι (rules 85, 9). The competing placement of that on τό is named in the article's note.
SBLGNT.ROM.4.13.v009 is underdetermined over s016 and the projection carries r00-base; no new textual decision is made here (rule 12).
